verdict.rationale: ScrapingBee's first-party docs say scraping a page needs only an API key and the encoded URL, and that the API returns the page's HTML, with optional waits or JS scenarios applied before it does. This delivers the single-call HTML retrieval the story describes. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the returned HTML, and an explicitly documented way to get unrendered raw source (JS rendering is on by default and images/CSS are blocked by default).

support.subject: As a developer, I can scrape a web page with a single API call and get its raw HTML back

citations.quote: To scrape a web page, you only need two things: Your API key... The encoded web page URL you want to scrape
Our headless browsers will wait for the CSS / Xpath selector passed in the parameter before returning the HTML.
If you want to interact with pages you want to scrape before we return your the HTML you can add JavaScript scenario to your API call.
